Program.cs must compose the app through IServiceCollection using SDK namespaces and one local composition namespace only.

What The Standard says

“entry point” — The Standard identifies the entry point and dependency registration as configuration responsibilities. Program.cs should remain a thin composition root that delegates domain registration through IServiceCollection. read it here.
“encapsulated” — The Standard's library example hides internal dependencies behind an encapsulated registration method and stable contracts. Restricting Program.cs to SDK namespaces and the local composition extension preserves that boundary. read it here.

Why it matters

Program.cs should remain a small composition script: create the host, call the local registration entry point, and start the app. Restricting its dependencies prevents business logic and layer knowledge from accumulating in the executable entry point.

Bad code example

// Violates STXAPP005: Program.cs must compose the app through IServiceCollection using SDK namespaces and one local composition namespace only.
using Schools.Controllers;
using Schools.Services;

WebApplicationBuilder builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

Good code example

// Follows STXAPP005
using Schools;

WebApplicationBuilder builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddSchools();
